svg.title: SAML 2.0 Single Sign-On
svg.desc: SAML 2.0 Single Sign-On. Enterprise SSO: the identity provider posts a signed assertion to the app through the browser. Step 1, SP sends an AuthnRequest: Expense has no session, so it redirects the browser to the IdP with an AuthnRequest (ID id-7f3a). Step 2, IdP posts the assertion: Ana signs in with password and MFA. The IdP posts a signed assertion to Expense via the browser. Step 3, Validate, map, then SSO: Expense checks the assertion and starts a session; Travel then gets its own, with no password. Step 4, IdP-initiated and risks: IdP-initiated: a portal click posts an assertion nobody asked for. Beware wrapping and rollover too.

g.text: Expense has no session, so it redirects the browser to the IdP with an AuthnRequest (ID id-7f3a).
Ana signs in with password and MFA. The IdP posts a signed assertion to Expense via the browser.
Expense checks the assertion and starts a session; Travel then gets its own, with no password.
IdP-initiated: a portal click posts an assertion nobody asked for. Beware wrapping and rollover too.
at sign-in the two servers never call each other
stale: the IdP now signs with cert B
front channel: every message goes through the browser
the XML deflated, base64- and URL-encoded
No request to match: one replay defence
fewer, so some apps refuse or restrict it.
A forged assertion slipped in beside the
signed one: act only on what the signature
The IdP switches to signing cert B. An SP
that hasn’t loaded the new metadata still
trusts only A and rejects every sign-in.
